opportunities.name: Open-source project lead research (HN + GitHub → note)
opportunities.description: For a given project name, search Hacker News for its top story, look up its GitHub repo for stars and latest release, then save a 'Lead' note summarizing both.
steps: Open HN search (hn.algolia.com) and select-all in the search box
Type {project} and press Enter
Read the top story title, points, and age
Open GitHub, click 'Search or jump to', type {project}, press Enter
Click the matching repository link ({owner}/{repo})
Read the star count and latest release date
Open the notes app, click 'New note'
Type 'Lead: {project}. HN "{top story title}" ({points} pts, {age}); GitHub {stars} stars, last release {date}' and press Enter

instances.values: project=deno (partial: only the GitHub search was seen, no HN search or note)
project=Bun, repo=oven-sh/bun (interrupted by CourtListener Tesla search)

opportunities.name: Company litigation story pitch (CourtListener + Wikipedia → email)
opportunities.description: For a given company, search CourtListener for a notable case, look up the company on Wikipedia for HQ and CEO, then draft a pitch email to an editor.
steps: Open CourtListener, click the 'Keyword(s) search with operators' box, select-all
Type {company} and press Enter
Open a relevant case result and note the case name, court, and filing date
Open Wikipedia, search {company}, and open the company article
Note the HQ and CEO
In the mail app, compose a new message to {recipient}
Set Subject to 'Pitch: {company} in court'
Write a body with the case name, court, filing date, HQ, and CEO, ending 'Worth a piece?'

instances.values: company=Uber, case=Uber v. Uber (Ohio Ct. App. 2017), recipient=lena@example.com (interrupted by IMDb browsing)
company=Tesla, Wikipedia 'Tesla, Inc.' (no email seen; interrupted by Bun lead research)

opportunities.name: Country fact-check (World Bank indicator + BBC context → note)
opportunities.description: For a given country, look up a World Bank indicator such as life expectancy, find a recent BBC news story on '{country} {topic}', and save a fact-check note.
steps: Open World Bank Data and dismiss any pop-up
Click the 'Search data e.g. GDP, population, Indonesia' box, type {country} using the World Bank spelling (e.g. 'Viet Nam'), and press Enter
Open the country page and read the indicator value and year (e.g. life expectancy at birth)
Open BBC, click 'Open menu', click the search box
Type '{country} {topic}' and press Enter
Open the most relevant recent article and note its headline and age
In the notes app, click 'New note' and type 'Fact-check {country}: {indicator} {value} ({year}). Context: {headline} ({age})', then press Enter

instances.values: country=Argentina (partial: repeated World Bank searches only)
